levels.title: Product and Vocabulary Foundations
levels.description: Describe Sonar, recognise the main products, and understand basic quality and security vocabulary.

questions.prompt: What is SonarQube primarily used for?

choices.label: Automated code quality and security verification

questions.prompt: Sonar in one sentence
questions.front: How would you describe Sonar to a new customer?
questions.back: Sonar helps teams verify that code is reliable, maintainable, and secure before it reaches production. It applies automated, explainable analysis across developer and AI-generated code.

questions.prompt: Which product gives feedback inside the editor?
Connected Mode
questions.front: What does Connected Mode add to SonarQube for IDE?
questions.back: Connected Mode binds the IDE workspace to a SonarQube project. It synchronizes team rules, project settings, issue statuses, and quality-gate notifications into the developer's editor.

questions.prompt: Which product is Sonar-managed SaaS?
Which product is self-managed by the customer?
Community Build
questions.front: What is SonarQube Community Build?
questions.back: SonarQube Community Build is the free, open-source self-managed SonarQube option. It is useful for starting with core code quality workflows, but it should not be confused with paid Server editions.

questions.prompt: What does static analysis inspect?

choices.label: Source code without running the application
Live production traffic and user sessions

questions.prompt: Rules and issues
questions.front: What is the relationship between a rule and an issue?
questions.back: A rule is a check; an issue is a finding raised when code violates that check. Quality Profiles decide which rules are active during analysis.

questions.prompt: Which issue category maps to reliability?
Which issue category maps to maintainability?
Vulnerability
questions.front: What is a vulnerability in Sonar vocabulary?
questions.back: A vulnerability is a security issue that can expose software to attack. It is different from a Security Hotspot, which requires human review before being treated as a problem.

questions.prompt: What does a Security Hotspot require?
Quality Gate
questions.front: What is a Quality Gate?
questions.back: A Quality Gate is a pass/fail policy based on conditions such as issues, ratings, coverage, or duplication. It tells teams whether code meets the required standard for merge or release.

questions.prompt: What does a Quality Profile define?

choices.label: The active rules for a language
The hosting region for a project

questions.prompt: AI-generated code
questions.front: Why does AI-generated code still need verification?
questions.back: AI-generated code can still contain bugs, vulnerabilities, and maintainability issues. Sonar's position is that independent verification is needed because generation and review should not be the same unchecked process.

questions.prompt: What is AI Code Assurance for?

choices.label: Applying stronger standards to projects with AI code
Training a new language model from scratch

questions.prompt: Sonar way
questions.front: What is Sonar way?
questions.back: Sonar way is Sonar's built-in recommended default for quality profiles and quality gates. It gives most teams a practical starting standard before customization.

levels.title: Development Workflow, Governance and Adoption
levels.description: Apply Sonar concepts across IDE, CI/CD, pull requests, new code, quality standards, and customer adoption.

questions.prompt: A team wants identical IDE and server rules. What helps?
IDE to CI
questions.front: How should a CSE explain IDE feedback versus CI analysis?
questions.back: IDE feedback helps developers fix issues before commit. CI analysis provides centralized verification, history, and enforceable quality gates for branches and pull requests.

questions.prompt: What does pull-request analysis focus on?

choices.label: Issues introduced by the pull request

questions.prompt: Pull-request decoration
questions.front: Why is pull-request decoration useful?
questions.back: It brings Sonar findings and Quality Gate status into the repository platform where developers already review code. This reduces context switching and makes governance visible before merge.

questions.prompt: Which pair is correctly distinguished?

choices.label: Profile selects rules; gate checks thresholds
Profile hosts code; gate edits code
Profile tracks sales; gate routes support

questions.prompt: What does a New Code Definition configure?

choices.label: Which changes count as new code
Which rules are active per language

questions.prompt: Clean as You Code
questions.front: Why is Clean as You Code practical for legacy codebases?
questions.back: It focuses strict standards on new or changed code instead of demanding full historical cleanup immediately. Teams improve the codebase incrementally while preventing new problems.

questions.prompt: A PR fails the Quality Gate. What happened?

choices.label: At least one gate condition was not met

questions.prompt: Coverage
questions.front: How should a CSE explain code coverage?
questions.back: Coverage estimates how much code is exercised by tests. It is useful for reliability discussions, but high coverage alone does not prove the code is bug-free.

questions.prompt: A customer needs self-managed data control. Which fits best?
A cloud-native team wants low operations. Which fits best?
Duplication
questions.front: Why does Sonar track duplication?
questions.back: Duplicated code can increase maintenance cost because the same logic may need to be fixed in several places. It is a code-health metric, not a direct security finding.

questions.prompt: Which signal best indicates adoption progress?

choices.label: Teams consistently using PR analysis and gates
A user opened the pricing page

questions.prompt: Technical success plan
questions.front: What should a technical success plan connect?
questions.back: It should connect the customer's business priorities to concrete technical actions, such as onboarding projects, enabling PR analysis, adopting quality gates, and measuring outcomes.

questions.prompt: Which is a likely customer-health risk signal?

choices.label: Quality Gate failures are ignored for releases

questions.prompt: Time to value
questions.front: What does time to value mean for Sonar adoption?
questions.back: Time to value is how quickly the customer sees useful outcomes from Sonar. Examples include visible PR feedback, fewer new issues, or clear quality-gate governance.

questions.prompt: What is the best early onboarding goal?

choices.label: Analyze a real project and review actionable findings
Customize every rule before first analysis

questions.prompt: CSE versus Support
questions.front: How is a Sonar CSE different from technical support?
questions.back: A CSE is a proactive technical advisor focused on adoption, maturity, health, and outcomes. Support usually reacts to specific incidents or product issues.

levels.title: Agentic Products and CSE Reasoning
levels.description: Explain Sonar's AI-code strategy and reason through realistic customer situations.

questions.prompt: Which sequence matches Sonar's AC/DC framing?
Zero-trust verification
questions.front: What does zero-trust verification mean for AI-generated code?
questions.back: It means the code generator should not be trusted to grade its own work. Sonar positions independent, deterministic verification as a separate check on AI-generated output.

questions.prompt: A customer wants agent-loop guidance and verification. Which product fits?
Sonar Vortex
questions.front: What customer problem does Sonar Vortex address?
questions.back: Sonar Vortex helps AI coding agents use project-specific context and verify output inside the agent loop. It targets agentic code quality before issues reach pull request or CI review.

questions.prompt: Which AC/DC stage does Remediation Agent support?
What does the SonarQube MCP Server connect?

choices.label: AI tools to SonarQube context and actions

questions.prompt: Context Augmentation
questions.front: How should you describe Context Augmentation in 2026?
questions.back: Context Augmentation provides repo-aware architecture, standards, and quality context to AI agents. Current Sonar sources describe it as included in Sonar Vortex, so its standalone terminology is time-sensitive.

questions.prompt: Which use case best fits Gitar?

choices.label: AI-native pull-request review and fix suggestions

questions.prompt: SonarSweep
questions.front: Why should SonarSweep be discussed carefully?
questions.back: SonarSweep is presented as early access or private beta around training-data quality and embedded context for coding LLMs. A CSE candidate should avoid positioning it like a mature, generally available SonarQube product.

questions.prompt: Which capability is added by Advanced Security?
A customer asks about vulnerable dependencies. Which concept fits?
Advanced SAST
questions.front: How does advanced SAST extend standard taint analysis?
questions.back: Advanced SAST extends data-flow analysis across dependency boundaries. It helps find vulnerabilities caused by interactions between first-party code and third-party libraries.

questions.prompt: Which scenario is the strongest CSE risk signal?

choices.label: AI-generated code bypasses quality gates before release
A champion requests an outcome review

questions.prompt: Maturity assessment
questions.front: What should a Sonar maturity assessment examine?
questions.back: It should examine how consistently the customer uses Sonar across IDE, CI/CD, PR review, quality gates, security workflows, and executive reporting. The goal is to identify practical next steps, not to score customers for its own sake.

questions.prompt: Which is the clearest expansion opportunity signal?

choices.label: Security leaders need dependency risk and SBOM visibility
A legacy issue is accepted as false positive

questions.prompt: Qualified Sales handoff
questions.front: When should a CSE hand an opportunity to Sales?
questions.back: A CSE should hand off when a signal is tied to a clear customer need, stakeholder, value hypothesis, and likely commercial motion. The handoff should be qualified, not just a vague mention of interest.

questions.prompt: A VP worries AI code increases outages. Best CSE follow-up?

choices.label: Ask how AI code is verified before merge today
Promise Sonar will eliminate all defects

questions.prompt: CSE versus Sales Engineering
questions.front: How is CSE different from Sales Engineering after purchase?
questions.back: Sales Engineering usually supports pre-sale technical evaluation. CSE works post-sale to drive adoption, maturity, customer health, and measurable outcomes while coordinating qualified commercial signals.
